html:
Suriname is a small country on the northern coast of South America, between Guyana and French Guiana. More than nine tenths of it is rainforest. It was a Dutch colony for three centuries and became independent in 1975.

English planters founded the colony in 1650. The Dutch seized it in 1667, and at the Peace of Breda that year each side kept what it held, so the Dutch kept Suriname while the English kept New Amsterdam, now New York.

Under the Dutch it became a plantation colony of sugar, coffee and cocoa along the rivers, worked by Africans brought through the Atlantic slave trade. Its regime was notoriously harsh. Many enslaved people escaped into the forest, and their descendants, the Maroons, won treaties of freedom in the 1760s and still live along the upper rivers.

Slavery ended in 1863. Planters then brought contract workers from British India and, from 1890, from Java. So Suriname is one of the most mixed countries in the world, with Hindu, Muslim, Christian and Maroon communities side by side. Bauxite mining became its main industry in the 1900s.

Independence came in 1975, and about a third of the people moved to the Netherlands around that time. Army officers led by Dési Bouterse seized power in 1980 and murdered fifteen critics in 1982. A war with Maroon rebels followed in the late 1980s. Democracy returned in the 1990s.
sum: Suriname is a small country on the northern coast of South America, between Guyana and French Guiana. More than nine tenths of it is rainforest. It was a Dutch colony for three centuries and became independent in 1975.
